items.title: How REST over-fetching grows as a screen needs more nested data
items.description: A mobile screen needs a user, their orders, and each order's line items — 3 levels of nesting. A REST endpoint typically returns the full resource shape at each level (no per-field selection), so response size grows with nesting depth even if the screen only displays a few fields. A GraphQL query asks for exactly the fields the screen uses, so its response size stays flat as nesting grows. Drag the nesting depth to see the two strategies diverge.

params.name: nestingDepth
params.label: Levels of nested data the screen needs

items.compute: const fieldsPerLevelRest = 10; const bytesPerField = 25; const fieldsScreenActuallyUses = 6; const restBytes = fieldsPerLevelRest * params.nestingDepth * bytesPerField; const graphqlBytes = fieldsScreenActuallyUses * bytesPerField; return { restBytesKB: Math.round(restBytes / 100) / 10, graphqlBytesKB: Math.round(graphqlBytes / 100) / 10 };

items.title: What it costs to keep old API versions alive
items.description: Every supported version needs its own test matrix, on-call knowledge, and review overhead for every future change — even if the version's own code barely changes. Drag the number of simultaneously-supported versions to see estimated monthly maintenance hours grow, using WeatherNow's own numbers as a starting point (v1 and v2, roughly the cost profile from this unit's scenario).
items.compute: const baseHoursPerMonth = 8; const perExtraVersionHours = 14; const extraVersions = Math.max(0, params.versionsSupported - 1); const maintenanceHours = baseHoursPerMonth + perExtraVersionHours * extraVersions; return { maintenanceHours };
